Requirement R05 (input): Report Intelligence Data. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to send intelligence data to the command/support chain..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-05.1, F-05.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-05.<F>.1, Be-05.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-05.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent:** Enable the pilot to transmit gathered intelligence data to the C2/support chain via the HMI (from use case 2.2).

Function candidates:

**F-05.1 — Transmit structured intelligence report.**
The purpose is to package and send a discrete intelligence finding (target ID, coordinates, classification, sensor tag) as a formatted report to C2. Function is *for* getting a complete, structured data record into the command chain. Measurable effect: a valid report is received by C2.

**F-05.2 — Confirm intelligence transmission integrity.**
The purpose is to give the pilot certainty that the intel actually reached C2 (send success/failure). Function is *for* closing the loop on delivery, not for composing the data. Measurable effect: pilot can distinguish sent vs. failed vs. pending.

**F-05.3 — Rapidly flag/mark an intel observation.**
The purpose is a low-effort "tag it now" capability — mark a finding of interest with minimal data so the pilot doesn't lose the observation while hands/attention are loaded, deferring full reporting. Function is *for* capturing perishable observations under high workload. Measurable effect: an observation is captured with minimal interaction cost.

These are genuinely distinct: F-05.1 is data authoring/dispatch, F-05.2 is delivery assurance, F-05.3 is fast capture. R05's stated intent ("send intelligence data") maps most directly to **F-05.1** — I'd lead with that. F-05.2 is arguably a shared behaviour candidate across all reporting requirements (R05, surveillance data, etc.), not exclusive here — flag it for later consolidation.

Which do you want to close on?
